figures.caption: Table 6: Per-trajectory streams written by the IMBENCH LeRobot recorder. Rates are configurable per category via recording.save_freq.*; values shown are typical defaults for a 100 Hz control loop. Cameras are stored as MP4 with per-row frame_index.* pointers in Parquet.

Table 8: Stage-1 understanding accuracy per task (%). A response is graded correct on a probe if it satisfies all required identifications and contains no forbidden false positives; task-level accuracy is the macro-average across applicable probes

Figure 1: IMBench — a benchmark for intuitive manipulation. Top: Each task is decomposed into a three-stage cognitive loop. Understand extracts latent physical properties from perception (e.g., a thin plate flush on a table affords no top-down grasp). Infer simulates forward dynamics and selects sub-goals (e.g., slide-then-grasp). Act executes a closed-loop interactive policy .

Table 2: Policy success rates (%) on IMBENCH, averaged over tasks within each category. Rollouts are over 20 seeds and 5 rollouts each. Bold marks the best entry per row. ZS = zero-shot pretrained checkpoint; FT = finetuned on teleoperation data. Diffusion Policy (DP) is trained from scratch (Full-training).
Table 15: Policy success rates (%) per task on IMBENCH. Bold marks the best per row.
Table 3: OOD generalization (task-wise). Success rate under in-distribution (ID) and out-ofdistribution (OOD) settings, with absolute drop ∆.

Figure 2: IMBench: 35 tasks across seven categories. Each targets a distinct inference bottleneck: geometry (P1), dynamics (P2), causal chains (P3), tool use (P4), hidden state (P5), reactive replanning (P6), stability (P7); two miscellaneous tasks in grey (bottom row).

Table 5: Master catalog of IMBENCH tasks. “Demos” lists curated counts after the three-stage filtering pipeline. A dash (–) in the teleop column denotes a task for which teleoperation is infeasible with the SpaceMouse interface.
Table 10: Stage-3 action success rate per task (%) for GPT-5.5 without and with privileged object context.
Table 9: Stage-2 plan correctness per task (%). Plans graded correct if a human verifier finds the generated plan sufficient to execute the task correctly.
